chunks: And Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who drove a sacrificial animal and did not garland it, nor mark it.
He عليه السلام said: "It has sufficed for him; very often it is neither garlanded, nor marked, nor covered."

key_terms.أَجْزَأَ: was sufficient and fulfilled the requirement
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial animal being driven as an offering
key_terms.يُجَلَّلُ: to be covered or adorned with a cloth
key_terms.يُقَلِّدْهُ: to place a garland on the sacrificial animal

ai.seo_question: Is a sacrificial animal valid if it was neither garlanded nor marked?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a sacrificial animal driven for hajj rites. It states that the offering is valid even if it was not garlanded or marked, indicating that these acts are not required for sufficiency in this case.
